Transfer functions

Source: R/physics-control-lti.R
TransferFunction.Rd

TransferFunction(num, den, var) is the continuous transfer function num/den in the complex variable var of the Laplace transform, and DiscreteTransferFunction(num, den, var, sampling_time) the discrete one in the variable of the z-transform. PIDController(kp, ki, kd, tf, var) is the transfer function of a PID controller with a derivative filter time constant tf. The class methods TransferFunction$from_rational_expression(expr, var), $from_coeff_lists(num_list, den_list, var) and $from_zpk(zeros, poles, gain, var) build transfer functions; the discrete class also has $from_gbt(), $from_bilinear(), $from_forward_diff() and $from_backward_diff(). A transfer function has the properties $num, $den, $var, $sampling_time, $is_proper, $is_strictly_proper and $is_biproper and the methods $poles(), $zeros(), $dc_gain(), $eval_frequency(other), $is_stable(), $to_expr(), $to_standard_form(), $simplify(), $expand() and $get_asymptotic_stability_conditions(). The operators +, -, *, / and ^ build Series(), Parallel() and Feedback() interconnections. After sympy.physics.control.lti.

Usage

TransferFunction(num, den, var)

DiscreteTransferFunction(num, den, var, sampling_time = 1)

TransferFunctionBase

PIDController(
  kp = Symbol("kp"),
  ki = Symbol("ki"),
  kd = Symbol("kd"),
  tf = 0L,
  var = Symbol("s")
)

Arguments

num, den

The numerator and denominator.

var

The complex variable.

sampling_time

The sampling time.

kp, ki, kd

The proportional, integral and derivative gains.

tf

The derivative filter time constant.

Value

A TransferFunction, DiscreteTransferFunction or PIDController object.

Examples

s <- Symbol("s")
G <- TransferFunction(s + 1, s^2 + 2, s)
G$poles()
#> [[1]]
#> sqrt(2)*I
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> -sqrt(2)*I
#> 
G * TransferFunction(1, s, s)
#> Series(TransferFunction(s + 1, s^2 + 2, s), TransferFunction(1, s, s))
TransferFunction$from_rational_expression((s + 1) / (s^2 - 1), s)
#> TransferFunction(s + 1, s^2 - 1, s)
